name: Wright State University
academic_ranking: Public research university (Carnegie R2: Doctoral Universities - High research activity), founded 1967 and named for the Wright brothers. Enrolls roughly 11,000+ students across seven colleges and three schools, offering ~106 bachelor's and ~136 graduate programs. Notable for the Boonshoft School of Medicine and engineering/computing programs. U.S. News national ranking approx. 230-301; Forbes approx. 198. Accredited by the Higher Learning Commission.
financial_aid: Public in-state undergraduate tuition and fees approx. $11,522/yr; out-of-state approx. $21,222/yr (NCES College Navigator, 2024-25). Wright State offers merit- and need-based institutional aid, federal/state grants, and athletic aid; softball athletic scholarships are administered within NCAA D1 equivalency limits. Prospective athletes should confirm current aid packages with the WSU financial aid office.
facilities_notes: Softball competes at the on-campus softball facility on the Wright State (Dayton-area) campus in Fairborn, OH. Specific facility name/capacity not verified from a live source at time of research; confirm via wsuraiders.com facilities pages.
program_reputation: NCAA Division I program competing in the Horizon League. Program has produced All-Horizon League players and has NCAA Tournament experience per assistant coach bio history. Led by head coach Laura Matthews.
notes: Data captured live from wsuraiders.com softball coaches page and roster page on 2026-07-30. Coaching staff consists of one head coach and two assistant coaches; no volunteer, graduate assistant, or director-of-player-development titles were listed for Wright State (note: an initial cached fetch mistakenly returned Youngstown State data via the shared Sidearm/Imperva CDN; that was discarded and re-fetched clean). Roster size of 17 reflects distinct player profiles on the softball roster page. No per-coach phone numbers or personal Twitter/X handles are published in the staff directory (team account is @WSU_SB). Tuition figures from NCES College Navigator (id 206604), 2024-25.
